title: Design exercise: SAA-3.1-S01
scenario: Harlow Bay Commodities runs a self-managed trade-ledger database on a single EC2 instance because its vendor supports only a block device, and the auditors want sustained performance evidenced before the year-end close. At the month-end peak the ledger issues about 45,000 I/O operations per second against a 2 TiB data set, each operation must average under 1 millisecond, and the auditors ask for the highest durability AWS publishes for a block volume. Separately, a nightly job reads one 12 TiB archive of transaction logs front to back in large sequential passes, every night, and must sustain 400 MiB/s. Neither volume is a boot volume, and both sit in one Availability Zone.
constraints: Do not claim live AWS experience
Finance requires the lowest-cost block storage type that still meets each workload's stated figures, so the two workloads need not share a type
The vendor will not support striping several volumes together into one device for the ledger
The auditors accept only figures published by AWS as evidence of the latency and durability claims

rubric.label: The ledger volume is shown to meet 45,000 IOPS, an average latency under 1 millisecond and the highest published volume durability, using published AWS figures
The log archive volume sustains 400 MiB/s at its 12 TiB size, the record cites the published throughput for that size, and the type chosen is the lowest-cost one that does
